questions.rationale: Prednisone tablet labeling: "Prednisone is a glucocorticoid," and each tablet contains 5, 10, or 20 mg. Rheumatic indications include adjunctive short-term use in rheumatoid arthritis.

questions.question: Tri-Sprintec is indicated to
questions.rationale: Tri-Sprintec is a norgestimate plus ethinyl estradiol combination oral contraceptive indicated for use by females of reproductive potential to prevent pregnancy.

questions.question: Combination oral contraceptives are contraindicated in
options: Women over 35 years of age who smoke
questions.rationale: Tri-Sprintec boxed warning: contraindicated in women over 35 who smoke, because smoking increases serious cardiovascular events from COC use.

questions.question: FDA lists St. John's wort as
options: A strong CYP3A inducer, with an effect that varies by preparation
A strong CYP3A inhibitor like grapefruit juice
A drug with no CYP effect
questions.rationale: FDA's CYP examples table lists St. John's wort as a dietary supplement and a strong CYP3A inducer. Footnote 18: the effect varies widely and is preparation dependent.

questions.question: Back-up contraception after stopping St. John's wort with a COC should continue for
questions.rationale: Tri-Sprintec §7.1 names products containing St. John's wort among agents that may decrease COC effectiveness, and says to continue back-up contraception for 28 days after the enzyme inducer is stopped.

questions.question: Biotin supplements are a problem because they can
options: Interfere with some lab tests, including falsely low troponin
Induce CYP3A4 like St. John's wort
questions.rationale: FDA: biotin in dietary supplements can significantly interfere with certain lab tests and cause incorrect results. FDA has received reports of falsely low troponin from biotin interference.

questions.question: Fosamax treatment of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women and men is
options: 10 mg daily or 70 mg once weekly
5 mg daily or 35 mg once weekly
questions.rationale: FOSAMAX dosage: treatment of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women and in men is 10 mg daily or 70 mg once weekly. Prevention in postmenopausal women is 5 mg daily or 35 mg once weekly.

questions.question: Adult Tamiflu treatment is
questions.rationale: TAMIFLU dosage: treatment of influenza in adults and adolescents 13 years and older is 75 mg twice daily for 5 days.

questions.question: Ozempic maintenance start after the initial 4 weeks is
questions.rationale: OZEMPIC is administered once weekly. Start at 0.25 mg once weekly;after 4 weeks increase to 0.5 mg once weekly. A missed dose may be administered within 5 days.

questions.question: The Lamictal XR boxed warning cites serious rash, including SJS, at about
options: 0.8% (8 per 1,000) in ages 2 to 16 and 0.3% (3 per 1,000) in adults on adjunctive epilepsy therapy
questions.rationale: LAMICTAL XR boxed warning gives those two rates for immediate-release lamotrigine used as adjunctive epilepsy therapy, and states XR is not approved for patients younger than 13 years.

questions.question: Allopurinol serious skin reactions, including SJS and TEN, occur in about
questions.rationale: Allopurinol tablets §5.1: TEN, SJS, and DRESS have been reported, occurring in approximately 5 in 10,000 (0.05%) patients. Discontinue permanently at the first skin rash.

questions.question: A serious cutaneous reaction in the Bactrim warnings is
options: Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis
Serotonin syndrome as the labeled skin warning
questions.rationale: BACTRIM Warnings: fatalities and serious adverse reactions include SCARs, including Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis.

questions.question: Ozempic is contraindicated in
options: A personal or family history of MTC, or MEN 2
questions.rationale: OZEMPIC boxed warning: rodent thyroid C-cell tumors;human relevance for MTC is not determined;contraindicated in personal or family history of MTC or in MEN 2.

questions.question: Victoza is contraindicated with
options: A personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma, or MEN 2
questions.rationale: VICTOZA boxed warning: rodent thyroid C-cell tumors;unknown whether it causes MTC in humans;contraindicated in personal or family history of MTC and in MEN 2.

questions.question: Oral acyclovir is indicated for
options: Only cold sores as the oral-tablet indications
questions.rationale: Acyclovir oral labeling: herpes zoster, initial and recurrent genital herpes, and chickenpox (varicella).

questions.question: Tamiflu treatment is for influenza symptoms that started no more than
questions.rationale: TAMIFLU is indicated for acute uncomplicated influenza A and B in patients 2 weeks and older who have been symptomatic for no more than 48 hours, and for prophylaxis in patients 1 year and older.

questions.question: Diflucan is indicated for
options: Vaginal candidiasis, oropharyngeal and esophageal candidiasis, and cryptococcal meningitis
questions.rationale: DIFLUCAN indications include vaginal candidiasis, oropharyngeal and esophageal candidiasis, and cryptococcal meningitis.

questions.question: Warfarin is
options: A direct thrombin inhibitor named in this label
questions.rationale: Warfarin sodium tablets are a vitamin K antagonist with those three labeled indication groups.

questions.question: Eliquis is
questions.rationale: ELIQUIS labeling: factor Xa inhibitor with those stroke, surgical-prophylaxis, and DVT/PE indications.

questions.question: Xarelto is
questions.rationale: XARELTO labeling identifies rivaroxaban as a factor Xa inhibitor and lists those indications in §1.1 through §1.5.

questions.question: An opened multi-dose vial with no manufacturer in-use date is discarded within
questions.rationale: CDC: once a multi-dose vial is opened (needle-punctured), date it and discard within 28 days unless the manufacturer states another date. The beyond-use date should never exceed the manufacturer's expiration date.

questions.question: Hazardous-drug storage areas must be
options: Kept on the public sales floor
Stored on the floor in the breakroom
questions.rationale: USP <800> §5: access to areas where HDs are handled must be restricted to authorized personnel. Designated areas must be available for storage of HDs.

questions.question: A multi-dose vial for more than one patient is kept
options: In a clean medication preparation area, away from immediate patient treatment areas
In the procedure-room cart for the whole day
In a patient room between cases
questions.rationale: CDC: multi-dose vials used for more than one patient should be kept and accessed in a clean medication preparation area away from immediate patient treatment areas. If one enters a treatment area, dedicate it to a single patient.

questions.question: Which oral class is on the ISMP acute-care high-alert list?
questions.rationale: The 2024 ISMP acute-care list names oral sulfonylurea hypoglycemics, with examples glimepiride, glipiZIDE, glyBURIDE, and TOLBUTamide.

questions.question: Which product is an ISMP community/ambulatory high-alert category?
options: pediatric liquid medications that require measurement
questions.rationale: The 2021 ISMP community/ambulatory list names pediatric liquid medications that require measurement, and immunosuppressants such as azaTHIOprine, cycloSPORINE, and tacrolimus.

questions.question: Humulin R U-500 concentration and syringe rule?
options: 500 units/mL, U-500 syringe only; a U-100 syringe can give a 5-times overdose
500 units/mL, draw it with a U-100 syringe and divide by 5
questions.rationale: Label: 500 units/mL is 5 times U-100 (100 units/mL). A U-100 syringe for a U-500 dose can give a 5-times overdose. Do not mix with other insulin or inject intravenously.

questions.question: HS on the ISMP error-prone list can mean:
options: half-strength or at bedtime — write the words
hour of sleep, and it is safe to abbreviate
questions.rationale: ISMP: HS half-strength mistaken as bedtime; hs at bedtime mistaken as half-strength. Write half-strength or bedtime.

questions.question: Which FDA tall-man pair is correct?
questions.rationale: FDA-approved tall-man list: buPROPion confused with busPIRone.

questions.question: Which is a required prospective DUR screen before the prescription is filled or delivered?
questions.rationale: 42 CFR 456.705(b) requires those seven screen types before the prescription is filled or delivered.

questions.question: Part D concurrent DUR is performed:
options: before each prescription is dispensed, usually at the point of sale
only after a quarterly claims audit
only after the patient reports harm
only when the prescriber requests a profile review
questions.rationale: 42 CFR 423.153(c)(2): concurrent DUR is before each prescription is dispensed, typically at the point of sale or point of distribution.

questions.question: Underutilization means:
options: insufficient quantity, strength, or duration to reach the therapeutic goal
a near miss caught at the counter
questions.rationale: 42 CFR 456.702 defines overutilization and underutilization with those quantity, strength, and duration terms.

questions.question: Which statement matches the FDA definitions?
options: A medication error may or may not be associated with an adverse event
Every adverse event is a medication error
Misuse inconsistent with the labeling is a medication error
An adverse event must be proven to be caused by the drug
questions.rationale: FDA guidance: an AE is any untoward medical occurrence associated with use of a drug product, whether or not considered related. A medication error may or may not be associated with an AE.

questions.question: Prospective DUR calculates daily dosage as:
questions.rationale: 42 CFR 456.705(b)(4): dosage is the strength multiplied by the quantity dispensed divided by day's supply.

questions.question: A suspected counterfeit or contaminated drug is reported to:
questions.rationale: FDA: report quality, authenticity, performance, or safety concerns to MedWatch, including suspect counterfeit, contamination, defective components, poor packaging or mix-up, questionable stability, and labeling concerns.

questions.question: Healthcare providers are required to report to VAERS:
options: an event on the VAERS Table of Reportable Events Following Vaccination within the specified time, and a manufacturer-listed contraindication to further doses
only events the patient asks to file
every sore arm, and nothing else may be reported
questions.rationale: CDC: providers must report table events within the specified time and manufacturer-listed contraindications to further doses. Anyone may report.

questions.question: CDC sequence for donning gown, mask, goggles, and gloves:
options: gown, mask or respirator, goggles or face shield, gloves
questions.rationale: CDC sequence: 1 gown, 2 mask or respirator, 3 goggles or face shield, 4 gloves over the gown wrist. Removal starts with gloves.

questions.question: When does CDC say to wash with soap and water rather than prefer an alcohol-based hand sanitizer?
options: hands visibly soiled, and care of patients with suspected or confirmed infection during C. difficile or norovirus outbreaks
before every tablet count, even when hands look clean
only after removing sterile chemo gloves
only at the start of the shift
questions.rationale: CDC: soap and water when visibly soiled and during those outbreaks. Unless visibly soiled, ABHS is preferred in most clinical situations.
